summary: Full regression of the post-refactor personal finance app (FastAPI + React, es-ES). Backend: created pytest suite /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (34 tests) covering health, dashboard KPIs/filters, transactions & card-transactions filters, CRUD (accounts, cards, categories, subcategories, rules), retroactive rule application (bank + card) on POST and PUT, refactored import parse-csv for .csv/.xls/.xlsx (amount parsing 1.234,56 vs Excel numeric, date normalization, auto-categorization by rules), import/confirm insert + dedup_hash duplicate skip, and inline categorization PUT endpoints. Result: 33 passed, 1 xfail (documented pre-existing regex bug). Frontend (Playwright, public preview URL): Dashboard (KPIs es-ES 1.339,71 €, Mes/Año actual toggle, month input incl. January, account filter), Income (Año+Mes filters, 'Sin categoría', search, Resumen por Categoría, export, inline category dropdown -> tx updated + automatic bank rule created), Expenses (same + expandable CategoryGroup with subcategory breakdown, subcategory filter), CreditCards (card select, 'Sin categoría', search by Concepto/Categoría, inline categorize -> tx updated + card rule created), ImportData 4-step wizard (upload .csv, preview, per-row category select proven to affect ONLY the targeted row across duplicate-concept rows => stable _rowKey confirmed, confirm inserts 3, re-import reports duplicates and DB stays at 3, wizard resets), Settings all 5 tabs + full create/edit/delete for accounts, cards, categories, subcategories, rules. Desktop + mobile drawer navigation verified. No console/page errors anywhere. Seeded DB integrity verified restored after tests (308 transactions, net_flow 1.339,71 €, no TEST_ leftovers).

minor.issue: `contains` is interpolated raw into MongoDB $regex without re.escape(). Concepts containing regex metacharacters (e.g. 'COMPRA *ESPECIAL* +X') silently match 0 transactions (applied_to_existing=0) and could also over-match. Verified reproducible; captured as xfail test test_rule_with_regex_metacharacters_in_concept. Fix: query['concept'] = {'$regex': re.escape(input.contains), '$options': 'i'} in both create_rule and update_rule.

category_id/subcategory_id are query params and `None` means 'do not update', so a category can never be cleared back to 'Sin categoría' from the UI. Also non-RESTful (mutating fields via querystring instead of a Pydantic body).

_parse_csv_text does {k.strip().lower(): v.strip()} — a CSV row with fewer columns than the header yields None values and raises TypeError, surfacing as a generic 400 'Error al procesar archivo: ...'. Guard with (v or '').strip().
Per-transaction failures are only counted in `errors` and logged; the response gives no detail about which rows failed, so the UI can silently drop rows.

integration_issues.issue: Every inline category change POSTs a new rule with the full concept as `contains` and no duplicate check, so the rules collection grows unbounded (already 51 rules). Combined with the unescaped-regex issue above, these auto-rules can silently apply to 0 rows. Consider upsert-by-(source, contains) instead of blind create.

issues: Bottom nav shows only 5 items (General, Ingresos, Gastos, Tarjetas, Importar) — 'Config' is reachable only through the hamburger drawer; acceptable but inconsistent with the desktop sidebar.
Contrast, spacing, alignment and footer/no-overflow all checked at 1920x1080 and 390x844 — no issues found.

action_items: Apply re.escape() to `contains` in create_rule and update_rule ($regex) so retroactive application works for concepts with regex metacharacters.
Allow clearing a category (support explicit null) on PUT /api/transactions/{id} and /api/card-transactions/{id}, ideally moving to a request body.
Harden _parse_csv_text against short rows (None values) before .strip().
De-duplicate auto-created rules from inline categorization (upsert by source+contains) to stop unbounded rules growth.

Optional code-quality: /app/backend/server.py (878 lines) and /app/frontend/src/pages/Settings.js (791 lines) both exceed the 700-line guideline — split server.py into routers (accounts/cards/categories/rules/transactions/import/dashboard) and move the 5 Settings tab components into their own files.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: rule `contains` flows straight into a $regex — this is both a correctness bug and an injection-style risk; escape it.

server.py: create_rule and update_rule contain ~40 lines of duplicated bank/card query-building and update logic — extract a single _apply_rule_to_existing(source, contains, sign, category_id, subcategory_id) helper (DRY).
server.py: the parse_csv refactor is behaviour-preserving and verified (csv/xls/xlsx, es-ES and Excel amount formats, rule auto-categorization, ISO date normalization all identical).

frontend: ImportData preview now keys rows by _rowKey and strips it before POST — verified end-to-end that editing one of two identical-concept rows does not affect its sibling and only the edited row's category is persisted.

frontend: all useEffect dependency arrays now reference stable useCallback refs; ESLint on /app/frontend/src reports zero issues in app code (only 3 pre-existing warnings inside untouched components/ui/calendar.jsx and command.jsx). No console.error/console.log left in app code.

success_rate.backend: 100% (33/33 passed, 1 xfail documenting a known pre-existing bug)

seed_data_creation: All test data was created via the API and deleted afterwards: TEST_ accounts, credit cards, categories, subcategories, rules, bank/card transactions and imported CSV rows (/tmp/test_import_ui.csv). Verified post-run: 308 transactions, 508 card transactions, 1 account, 1 card, 23 categories, 20 subcategories, 51 rules, dashboard net_flow 1.339,71 € — identical to the pre-test seeded state, zero TEST_ leftovers.
test_credentials: N/A - app has no authentication; /app/memory/test_credentials.md does not exist (not required for this app).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (+ conftest.py providing BASE_URL from /app/frontend/.env). It is self-cleaning via the module-scoped `cleanup` fixture — always register created ids there. Run: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest backend_test.py -v. The refactor itself (parse_csv helpers, useCallback/useMemo deps, extracted TransactionRow/ExpenseRow/CategoryGroup/Settings tabs, ImportData _rowKey) is fully verified with no behaviour regressions. I added data-testid='category-group-{id}' / 'category-group-header-{id}' to Expenses CategoryGroup. Remaining open items are all pre-existing (not refactor-caused): unescaped $regex in rules, inability to clear a category, unbounded auto-rule creation. Note the seeded data is all in 2025; 'Año actual' on the Dashboard shows 2026 and therefore 0,00 € — that is correct behaviour, not a bug.
rca_of_the_issue: Rules regex: create_rule/update_rule build query['concept'] = {'$regex': input.contains, '$options': 'i'} using the user/UI-supplied concept verbatim. Repro: POST /api/transactions with concept 'COMPRA *ESPECIAL* +X', then POST /api/rules with contains equal to that concept -> HTTP 200 but applied_to_existing = 0 because '*'/'+' are treated as regex quantifiers rather than literals. Mitigation: re.escape() the value before building the $regex (both endpoints). Impact is limited to retroactive application; the inline UI flow still updates same-concept transactions directly via PUT, which is why the visible UI behaviour looked correct.
